reasons: The SAVED and DRAFTING marks can fail for results with no LinkedIn link or email. The save key and the display key are built differently, which reads as a bug.
Two search types have the same draft buttons written out twice, so a change must be made in both places.
A contact can be saved even when its draft fails.
No tests are visible. Search and draft errors are caught and shown to the user.

terms.meaning: A private code a web service gives you so your app can use that service. Anyone holding it can use your account, so it must be kept private.
A waiting list where drafted messages sit until the user reviews and sends them.
A first message sent to someone who has not heard from you before.

sections.name: File setup, SearchType
sections.title: Imports and search types
sections.what: Brings in the tools this panel needs: application data, the user profile, contact saving, saved keys, message writers and the message queue. Also defines the four search types: hiring manager, referral candidate, CEO and executive.
sections.why: Keeps the panel's options defined in one place.
sections.watch_out: Adding a search type means changing several lists in this file by hand, including its label, its buttons and its draft options.

sections.name: ContactCard
sections.title: Shape of a search result
sections.what: Describes one search result: name, title, company, LinkedIn link, email, location, source (Exa or Apollo), confidence (high, medium or low) and a short snippet.
sections.why: Gives every result the same fields so display and saving code can rely on them.
sections.watch_out: The source and confidence values are fixed choices, so the server must send exactly these words.

sections.name: SEARCH_LABELS
sections.title: Search type button labels
sections.what: Maps each search type to the short capital label on its button: HIRING MANAGER, REFERRAL, CEO and EXECUTIVE.
sections.why: Keeps the display names separate from the internal type names.
sections.watch_out: Each search type needs an entry here. The TypeScript checker should flag a missing one.

sections.name: ContactsPanel (part 1)
sections.title: Panel memory and contact search
sections.what: Holds the panel's state: the chosen search type, results, loading flag, error message, which draft is being written, and which contacts are already saved. The search action first checks that a key is saved. If none is, it shows a message asking the user to add one in settings. Otherwise it sends the company, job title, location and keys to the server and shows up to 10 results.
sections.why: The check stops a request that cannot succeed and gives the user a clear next step.
sections.watch_out: Every search sends the saved provider keys to the server, so the server route must handle them carefully.

sections.name: ContactsPanel (part 2)
sections.title: Saving a contact and writing a draft
sections.what: When the user picks a draft action, the contact is first saved to the contacts list linked to this application and marked as saved. Then the matching message is written by AI and placed in the inbox queue. A failure shows a 'Draft failed' message. The drafting flag is cleared in every case.
sections.why: Likely reason: saving first keeps the contact even if the AI step fails.
sections.watch_out: The contact is saved before the AI step runs, so a failed draft still leaves a saved contact and no queued message.

sections.name: ContactsPanel (part 3)
sections.title: Search buttons and result cards
sections.what: Shows the four search type buttons and a SEARCH button, then any error message. Each result is a card with name, title, location, confidence and source badges, snippet, and links to LinkedIn or email. Results already saved show a SAVED mark. The result list scrolls when long.
sections.why: Lets the user switch search types and compare results quickly.
sections.watch_out: The SAVED and DRAFTING marks can fail to appear on results with no LinkedIn link or email. See the risks note.

sections.name: ContactsPanel (part 4)
sections.title: Draft buttons by search type
sections.what: Shows different draft buttons for each search type. Hiring managers and executives get DRAFT EMAIL and DRAFT DM. Referral candidates get DRAFT REFERRAL DM. CEOs get a red DRAFT CEO COLD EMAIL button. A note at the bottom says drafted messages appear in the inbox at the top right.
sections.why: Each kind of contact needs a different style of outreach.
sections.watch_out: The hiring manager and executive button sets are written out twice. A change to one usually needs the same change to the other.

sections.name: smallLink
sections.title: Small link style
sections.what: The look of the LinkedIn and email links on result cards: small monospace text inside a thin bordered box.
sections.why: Keeps the links consistent across cards.

sections.name: draftBtn
sections.title: Draft button size
sections.what: Sets the small size and padding used by the draft buttons.
sections.why: Keeps the draft buttons compact when several sit side by side.

summary: A panel that searches outside sources for people at a job's company, lets the user save the ones they pick, and asks AI to write an outreach message to each.
purpose: Helps the user find a hiring manager, referral candidate, CEO or executive to contact about a specific application, and queues the drafted message for review in the inbox.
why: Likely reason: keeps outreach tied to each application so the user can track who they contacted. The reason for this exact flow is not stated in the code.
how: 1. The user picks a search type. 2. The search function checks that an Exa or Apollo key is saved in settings, then asks the server for up to 10 people at the company. 3. Each result card shows its details and draft buttons that depend on the search type. 4. Pressing a draft button runs saveAndDraft, which saves the contact to the contacts list linked to this application. 5. The AI writes the message. 6. The message is placed in the queue for the inbox.
inputs: The application (company, job title, location), the user profile, the saved search keys, the chosen search type, and button presses.
outputs: A list of contact cards, new saved contacts, AI-written drafts placed in the inbox queue, and error messages shown under the search buttons.
risks: Saved search keys are sent to the server with every search. A contact is saved before its draft is written, so the contact can exist even when the draft fails. Results with no LinkedIn link or email get SAVED and DRAFTING marks that do not appear, which looks like a bug. Whether repeated saves of one person create duplicates depends on addContact, which is not in this file.
debug: If search asks for a key, check the integration settings. If no results appear, read the message under the search buttons and the server response for the search route. If a SAVED or DRAFTING mark is missing, check whether the result has a LinkedIn link or email. If a draft never reaches the inbox, look for the 'Draft failed' message and check the AI step and the queue functions in lib/notifications.
